title: The first program was written for a machine that never existed

panels.text: London, 1843. Ada Lovelace, daughter of the poet Lord Byron, translates a paper about Charles Babbage's planned Analytical Engine, a mechanical computer.
She adds seven long notes of her own. In the last, Note G, she lays out step by step how the machine could calculate a series of Bernoulli numbers.
That method is often called the first published computer program. The twist: the Analytical Engine was never finished, so her program was never run.
She also imagined more than arithmetic: a machine that could work with any symbols, perhaps even music. That idea took about a century to come true.
